LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To describe people’s appearance.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#9 Prepositions Actions Song
•	 TR#16 Thief Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home Song
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 1: A3 Blank Face (P.3.1) + 
Face cutouts + Blu-Tack
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 3: Bingo cards (P.3.2) + Bingo 
boards (P.3.3) + counters 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 10: Parts of the Face cutouts+ 
Blu-Tack
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 11: Number cards (P.E.M.3) 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 8: Character (P.3.2) + Age 
cards (P.3.8) 
•	 Big Book
•	 P&P Story 3 Student Books
•	 Day 1 stickers (1 per child)
•	 Crayons or pencils
•	 Blu-Tack
BEFORE CLASS
Prepare and label your Ss’ material beforehand.
•	 Prepare and label the right number of Story 3 Student 
Books.
•	 Tear the Story 3 stickers through the dotted line.
Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed 
Mission 2.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (11’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets 
•	 Calendar
•	 My Pet

2.– STORY (PP.2-6) (8’)
Tell the students the first half of the story using the Big 
Book. Please see the section on storytelling in the Warm-Up 
Routines Index.
3.– WORKSHEET: DESCRIPTIONS (P.3) (8’)
Descriptions
3
P.3.2
Michelle
MATERIALS:
•	 Crayons or pencils
Give out the student books saying, “Look! These are your 
student books for Story 3: The Thief!” and have the Ss ask you 
for the book by saying, “Can I have my book, please?”
This worksheet shows six characters from Activity 2. Ss must 
listen to the description of a character and write a number next 
to them. Ss will not be familiar with the characters yet, so you 
can help them as needed or place the A5 Cards (P.3.2) on the 
table for reference.
Start by describing a character by saying, for example, “This 
person has got long (straight*) blonde hair. This person is 
wearing glasses, a red jumper, a pair of blue jeans and a pair 
of green shoes.” Try not to say whether the character is male 
or female to make it more difficult. Then ask, “Who is it?” and 
the Ss must respond for example, “It’s Michelle/It’s her!” while 
pointing to the correct character.
Then you should say, “Please write number 59 next to 
Michelle.” You can use any number between 50 and 99. Circulate 
to make sure they are writing the correct numbers. 
KEY (Names of characters, left to right, top to bottom)
Lisa
Kyle
Mark
Jason
Michelle
Susie

> Follow-Up
Ask your Ss, “Who is number 63? What does this person 
look like?” and encourage them to describe that character by 
saying, “Person number 63 is X (name of the character). X 
has got short curly* brown hair, big blue eyes, small ears, a 
big nose and a small mouth. He’s wearing glasses, a red and 
blue jumper, a pair of green trousers and yellow trainers.” 
NOTE: as previously mentioned, students are not expected 
to produce such long descriptions. At minimum they should 
be able to describe the length and colour of the hair and use 
the “has got” structure properly.

5.– ACTIVITY 1: MAKE A FACE (VERSION 1) (9’) 
P.3.1
> Warm-Up
Present the vocabulary by playing a TPR game. Show the 
corresponding cutouts and ask Ss to point at someone who 
has the characteristic you are presenting. Keep it fast paced 
and avoid playing for over two minutes.

•	 Using the big/small eyes and ears cutouts: who has 
got big/small eyes/ears?
•	 Using three differently coloured eyes: who has got blue/
green/brown eyes?
•	 Using three differently coloured hair cutouts: who has 
got blonde/brown/black/red hair?
•	 Using two hair cutouts with different lengths: who has 
got short/long hair?
•	 Using three cutouts with different hair textures: who 
has got straight/wavy/curly hair?
•	 Using the moustache cutout: who has got a moustache?
> Main Activity
Tell your Ss, “It’s time to meet a new friend!”. Use Blu-Tack 
to place the A3 sheet on the whiteboard. Ask your Ss, “What 
is this person’s name?”, and have them choose a name for 
the character. You can write it on the A3 using an erasable 
whiteboard marker.
Then ask the whole group questions about the person’s 
appearance and place the cutouts accordingly. You should 
ask questions like the following, adapting the pronouns where 
needed:
•	 “Has he/she got big eyes or small eyes?” to which the 
Ss should reply, “He/she has got big eyes.” 
•	 “What colour are his/her eyes?” to which they should 
reply, “His/her eyes are blue.” 
Continue asking different questions and placing the cutouts 
until the whole face is done. 
> Follow-Up
When your character has been created, ask different Ss to 
describe them, “What does he/she look like?”, and the S should 
respond by saying one thing about the character. For example, 
“He/she has got short black hair.”
NOTE: if your group struggles coming up with such long 
descriptions, it’s advisable to stick to shorter ones such as, 
“She has got long blonde hair,” instead of saying “She has 
got long straight blonde hair.” There are many variables to 
pick, and the correct adjective order might seem difficult to 
Ss. This applies to the Oral Test as well.

6.– ACTIVITY 3: GUESS WHO BINGO (9’)
P.3.3
Charlie
Jason
Michelle
Joe
P.3.2
Joe
> How to Play
This game is a mix of the classic games Bingo and Guess 
Who. Take a character from the individual playing cards (P.3.2) 
at random and describe them to the Ss. Then they will have to 
guess who the character is and identify them on their boards. The 
S who finds the most characters by the end of the game, wins.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the target language. Take a character, show 
them to the Ss and describe them by saying for example, “This 
is Joe. He has got short (curly) grey hair, small brown eyes, 
a big nose, small ears, a moustache and a small mouth. He 
is wearing a green shirt, a blue cardigan, a pair of trousers 
and a pair of blue shoes.”
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s see if you can find 
all the characters on your board!”. Give each S a Bingo board 
(P.3.3) and shuffle the Playing cards (P.3.2). Choose one of the 
cards without the Ss seeing it. First, the Ss ask you, “What 
does this person look like?”, and you describe the character 
by saying, for example, “This person has got short (curly*) 
brown hair, big brown eyes, a small mouth and big ears. This 
person is wearing glasses. He is also wearing a red and blue 
(striped) jumper and a green pair of trousers.”. The Ss who 
have the character on their board should say, “It’s Kyle. I’ve 
got Kyle. Can I have a counter please?”. Play until you run out 
of time or until a S completes their board.
NOTE: you can either use counters or a whiteboard marker 
to cross out the characters on the boards. Make sure you wipe 
them clean afterwards.
> Follow-Up
The S with a full board (or the most counters) should choose 
one of the characters on their board and describe it. For example, 
the S may choose Susie and say, “Susie is wearing a blue hat.

She has got long red hair, big green eyes, a big nose and a big 
mouth. She is wearing a green dress and a blue hat.”
NOTE: once Ss are used to playing this game, you can ask a 
volunteer to take the cards, describe the characters, and give 
out counters. If your group struggles coming up with such long 
descriptions, it’s advisable to stick to shorter ones such as, “She 
has got long blonde hair,” instead of saying, “She has got long 
straight blonde hair”. We know that there are many variables 
to pick, and the correct adjective order might seem difficult to 
Ss. This will be applied to the Oral Test as well.
7.– ACTIVITY 10: DESCRIPTIONS SONG (TR#17) (5’)
> Warm-Up
One by one, show Ss the face parts cutouts and ask the Ss 
a question about their appearance. For example, show them 
the big blue eyes cutout and ask, “Jane, have you got big blue 
eyes?”. Encourage the S to respond “Yes, I have.” or “No, I 
haven’t. I have got...”
Try to ask each S at least one question. 
> Main Activity
Stick up the individual blonde, black, long, short, curly and 
straight hair cutouts on the whiteboard or place them on the 
table before you play the track. For the eyes and mouth, you 
can just use gestures. 
Every time you sing “Are you…?” hold up the palms of your 
hands in the air and then point in front of you when you say 
“You”. Then perform the action as indicated in brackets below.
DESCRIPTIONS SONG
Are you young? 
(smile and imitate rocking a baby in your arms)
Are you old? 
(bend over and walk as if you are an elderly person with 
a walking stick)
Are you short? 
(put your hands down low)
Or are you tall? 
(put your hands up high)
Have you got big eyes?
(point to your eyes and make a big circle with your hands)
Or have you got small eyes?
(point to your eyes and make a small circle with your hands)
What do you look like? 
(point to anybody)

Tell me something more, I’d like to know! 
(point to yourself first and then hold up your hands 
indicating that you don’t know)
Have you got blonde hair? 
(point to the cutout)
Have you got black hair? 
(point to the cutout)
Is it long or short, curly or straight?  
(point to the cutouts) 
What do you look like? I think I know! 
(put your palms facing up then to your eyes and finish 
by pointing to your head)
8.– ACTIVITY 11: NUMBERS (VERSION 1) (5’)
P.E.M.3
55
> Main Activity
The goal of the game is to find as many cards as possible. 
Stick some of the Number cards (P.E.M.3.) on the wall (out 
of reach of the Ss, so they can’t damage them). Say, “Find 
number...” and have the Ss run and point to the corresponding 
number. When the S points to the correct number, take it off 
the wall and keep it as a point for that S. The S who collects 
the most cards wins. 
NOTE: this game can become hectic if everybody is playing 
at the same time. It is advisable to play this game in duels of 
two Ss (S1 vs S2). You call out the number and the two Ss must 
race to point to the card first.

Introduce the new Mission by saying, “Mission 3 starts today!”. 
Remind your Ss to listen to the audio and to do the activities

10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG (TR#9)
> Main Activity
Play the Prepositions Actions Song (TR#9) and dance to it. 
PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG
(as you sing, simply perform the actions mentioned in the song. 
You can also create a hand choreography for the preposition 
verses.) 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
March in line, in, in line. 
(musical interlude)
Hide under the table, under, under the table.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Walk next to a friend, next to, next to a friend. 
(musical interlude)
Stand between two chairs, between, between two chairs.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.

Jump behind the teacher, behind, behind the teacher. 
(musical interlude)
Run in front of the board, in front of, in front of the board.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Sit on a chair, on, on a chair. 
(musical interlude)
This is the end, the end, the end.
ACTIVITY 8: HOW OLD ARE YOU?
P.3.2
Lisa
P.3.8
15
Lisa
> How to Play
Ss have to guess the age of a character by asking questions.
> Main Activity
Ss must guess the age of the different characters. Prepare 
two sets of cards, one with the character’s age (P.3.8) and one 
without (P.3.2). Choose a pair of cards of the same character, 
keep the age card in your hand and put the character card 
face up on the table for the Ss to see. Introduce the activity by 
saying, “Let’s see if you can guess how old the characters are!”.
If you take the Nancy card, for example, you can start by 
asking, “How old is Nancy?” and Ss must take it in turns asking, 
“Is she 20 years old?”, for example. You should then respond, 
“No, she isn’t.” and encourage Ss to ask, “Is she younger or 
older?” to which you should respond “She is older.”. When they 
are ready to guess the character’s age, they should ask, “Is she 
… years old?”. Once the Ss have guessed correctly, show the 
card with the age of the character and let one of the Ss have 
a turn at choosing a card.
